core_claim.quote: That recurrent processing is necessary for visual awareness is now fairly well established, and supported by numerous experiments

source.citation: Lamme VAF. How neuroscience will change our view on consciousness. Cognitive Neuroscience 1(3):204-220, 2010 (discussion paper; commentaries and response follow on pp. 220-240)

prediction.statement: In scalp EEG, seeing a stimulus first shows up as a negative wave over the back of the head about 200 ms after it appears (the 'visual awareness negativity'), the typical timing of recurrent processing in visual cortex, before the late positive wave (the P300) that comes with access and report.

first_stated.passage: Various manipulations of conscious perception consistently show to influence EEG activity in the 200 ms latency range—known as the visual awareness negativity (VAN)—which is the typical latency of recurrent visual processing [46].

source.citation: Lamme VAF. Challenges for theories of consciousness: seeing or knowing, the missing ingredient and how to deal with it. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 373:20170344, 2018

prediction.test_for: With the stimulus matched, seen and unseen visual stimuli differ in a negative wave over posterior (visual) scalp sites in roughly the 150 to 300 ms window, beginning before any late positive difference.
prediction.test_against: With the stimulus matched, no awareness-related difference appears before the late positive wave: the first reliable difference between seen and unseen stimuli comes after about 300 ms.

what_the_sources_say_about_rivals.statement: Global workspace theory's proponents place conscious appraisal in late events, the P300 above all, and say the first 200 ms can be the same whether or not a stimulus is consciously perceived.

source.citation: Mashour GA, Roelfsema P, Changeux J-P, Dehaene S. Conscious processing and the global neuronal workspace hypothesis. Neuron 105(5):776-798, 2020

other_statements_of_the_prediction.passage: In sum, recurrent interactions between visual neurons expressed as contextual modulation at the single neuron level or as 200 ms latency EEG signals (VAN) or PPI in humans, is crucial for the emergence of conscious experience.

source.citation: Lamme VAF. Challenges for theories of consciousness: seeing or knowing, the missing ingredient and how to deal with it. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 373:20170344, 2018

other_statements_of_the_prediction.passage: Eventually, recurrent interactions spread through the whole brain, causing ‘global ignition’. At the neural level this is expressed in P300 responses, and the involvement of fronto-parietal areas. The result is access (A-) consciousness

source.citation: Lamme VAF. Challenges for theories of consciousness: seeing or knowing, the missing ingredient and how to deal with it. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 373:20170344, 2018
